subject: Reserved GPU Fleet — commit term & pricing sensitivity
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@finexsys.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Bauer <tom.bauer@finexsys.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity inquiry — long-term commit and price protection

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran some internal load projections and want to explore a reserved capacity agreement for our inference fleet. High level: we expect to run two heavy LLM routes (conversational + reranker) with steady-state throughput roughly equivalent to ~40 H100 GPUs (model mix + batching). We have three asks before procurement will move to a PO:

- A recommended dedicated sizing plan (GPU counts, burst options) and an ops handoff plan.
- Pricing for 24- and 36-month reserved commits (and whether you can do quarterly invoicing).
- A mechanism to protect us if GPU OEM list prices drop significantly during the term (we'd like a price-pass or renegotiation clause if supplier price drops >10%).

Procurement is sensitive to unit economics: if we can get demonstrable savings at 36 months we can commit sooner. Can you share a proposal and any relevant attachments?

Best,
Elena

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity inquiry — long-term commit and price protection

Elena — thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a first-pass sizing workbook (redwood-dedicated-sizing-v2.xlsx) with an H100-equivalent baseline and two scenarios (steady-state and peak-burst). Quick summary below:

- Recommended commit: 60 H100-equivalent GPUs as a blended reserved pool (covers steady-state + buffer).
- Burst pool: 20 GPUs (on-demand or dedicated burst) for spiky workloads; automated fallback to hosted models if burst exceeds threshold.
- 24-month price example (list): $8,900 / GPU-month (H100-equivalent).
- 36-month price example (list): $8,100 / GPU-month (H100-equivalent).

You asked about sensitivity to OEM (NVIDIA) price moves. Our standard approach is a contract clause that allows for pass-through or adjustment if vendor OEM unit costs move >10% materially for the capacity profile. We can present two options:

A) Fixed unit price for the full term with a one-time renegotiation window if OEM prices drop >10% (customer-favored).
B) A shared-savings model: we apply an agreed % of any GPU vendor list-price decrease as a rebate to you quarterly.

I'll loop in our solutions and pricing leads internally to confirm what discounting we can commit to before I send a formal term sheet. If you prefer, we can also show a sliding discount schedule by commit term (12/24/36 months).

Next step: I'll pull together an internal approval request for discount tiers and a draft contract. Would a 36-month sliding discount schedule be most helpful for procurement to review?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer

Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity inquiry — approval request (discount / term)

Team — forwarding Elena's ask and the sizing workbook. Key commercial points: FinexSys wants a 24/36 month reserved commit; they're price-sensitive and specifically want a protection mechanic if OEM GPU list prices decline. High-level numbers from my initial pass: list-ish $8.9k (24m) / $8.1k (36m) GPU-month (H100-equivalent). They'd like an aggressive discount (they implied ~25–30%) for a 36-month lock.

Requesting guidance:
- Approve up to what % discount for a 36-month commit without escalation?
- Are we comfortable with a pass-through clause that triggers when NVIDIA list pricing changes by >10% (we need legal input on language)?
- Can we offer a blended commit of 60 H100-equivalent GPUs + 20 burst GPUs and hold to SLA?

I attached the pricing sensitivity model (pricing-sensitivity-model.csv) that shows margin impact at tiered discounts. If we go beyond ~20% discount on list, margin drops below threshold where leadership sign-off is required.

Markus / Grace — any notes on operational risk for the burst pool or suggested guardrails?

Thanks,
Karthik

[Attachment: pricing-sensitivity-model.csv (text/csv)]

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated capacity inquiry — approval request (discount / term)

Karthik — thanks for the thorough notes and the sensitivity sheet. Quick guidance from GTM/leadership:

- Approve up to 20% off the 36-month list price for committed deals in this tier without running to the CRO. For anything >20% we need a CRO/finance approval (please create a short deal memo).
- Approve the 60 H100-equivalent commit + 20 GPU burst architecture; include an automatic capacity reconciliation every quarter and a 30-day notice for any burst >50% of baseline.
- Contract language: legal should draft a clause with two options: (1) price-lock with a renegotiation trigger if OEM price drops >12% (customer can request renegotiation), or (2) a shared-savings rebate where we pass back 40% of realized supplier list-price decreases quarterly. The shared-savings route is preferred for larger customers but needs finance modeling.
- We should avoid open-ended pass-throughs tied to OEM list prices without a floor and cap. Suggest floor of 12-month equivalent and a cap at 30% pass-through exposure.

Please draft a one-page commercial memo for CRO sign-off if the final discount request exceeds 20%. Loop Legal on the proposed language in contract-term-draft.pdf. Also include an explicit exit/cancellation clause tied to usage thresholds and early termination fees for partial consumption of reserved pool.

- Ops note for Grace: ensure SRE sizing aligns with 60 + burst plan and that we can support the KV cache and batching expectations at that scale.

Markus
SVP, Global Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Proposal: Reserved fleet terms & next steps (RDW-FT-4821)

Elena — thanks for your patience. Per internal guidance I've summarized an offer below for FinexSys. This reflects leadership-approved guardrails and options for price-protection: 

1) Sizing & architecture
- Committed pool: 60 H100-equivalent GPUs (covers expected steady-state + buffer).
- Burst pool: 20 GPUs available on-demand; quarterly reconciliation and 30-day notice for sustained burst >50% of baseline.

2) Pricing (H100-equivalent, GPU-month)
- 24-month committed: $8,200 / GPU-month list; standard discounted rate we can offer on request.
- 36-month committed: $7,380 / GPU-month list.
- Leadership-approved discount: up to 20% off list for 36-month deals without CRO escalation. That yields an effective rate of $5,904 / GPU-month at the 20% tier.

3) Price-protection options (choose one)
A) Fixed-price with renegotiation trigger: If Nvidia list prices decline >12% for the capacity profile, FinexSys may open a renegotiation window (mutual good faith).
B) Shared-savings rebate: Redwood will pass 40% of realized vendor list-price decreases back to FinexSys, calculated quarterly, subject to a floor/cap (floor 5%, cap 30% total exposure).

4) Legal & billing
- Standard 36-month Master Services Agreement (attached). Quarterly invoicing available. Early termination fees apply for partial consumption; language in contract-term-draft.pdf.

5) Next steps
- If this structure is acceptable, we'll prepare a one-page commercial memo for CRO sign-off (required only if you request >20% discount).
- We'll route the contract to DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/doc/ABC-123.

Please let me know which price-protection option you prefer and whether you want us to model a blended H100/A100 equivalent. Once we have confirmation I will pull the final term sheet and get Legal to circulate the redlined MSA.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
